title: ml_entry runs on every account by config (one implementation, never a fork): parametrise the bybit/crypto-only assumptions found in #22079 so alpaca_live (and any account) can roster the SAME leg
note: Filed 2026-11-01 ~10:45Z by lane ML-ENTRY-GOLIVE-UNBLOCK (session_01AFoLuKfE1ZQzYVUj5a432n) on the manager's instruction (Manager Session 2026-11-01a). OPERATOR ~10:40Z, VERBATIM: "really, the same entry model should be applied to alpaca as to bybit 2 - we're trying to consolidate so we have overall-context models, in addtion to the per-symbol models, and I'm not sure when we decided that there was a distinction between bybit and the other accounts on this, but that's wrong - the supra-symbol mls are for all symbols on all accounts. If we find evidence for per-category MLs later on, than we'll build those later on, but that was never the design spec for the models I asked for this morning". #22079 keeps its scope (bybit_2 + bybit_portfolio). AUDIT of #22079 head 09df3fd (code read, not run on alpaca): on a non-Bybit account ml_entry would REFUSE every decision (safe: no wrong trade, but it never trades). Hard-coded items: (1) src/runtime/ml_decision_features.py:76,83-84 the BTCUSDT anchor literal (btc_ret24 / btc_vol24 features, and the row is unformable without it). (2) src/runtime/strategy_signal_builders.py _ml_entry_reference_frames: the 60 crypto reference symbols come from the artifact (meta.xs_reference) and are fetched with the TRADED symbol's exchange client, keeping only frames whose last bar ts equals the decision bar. An Alpaca client cannot list the perps, and equity bars never share the crypto bar ts, so n_reference=0 < min_reference_symbols 40 -> refuse. The module cache _ML_ENTRY_REF_CACHE is keyed on bar time only, not venue (two venues would share frames). Needed: a per-account reference source (venue + universe) independent of the trading venue. (3) src/units/strategies/ml_entry.py:50 is_decision_bar is UTC hour % 4 on 24/7 bars; market hours are not modelled (equity 1h bars, session open/close). The generic market_closes_before_max_hold refusal (strategy_signal_builders ~6294) already exists for the 24h time stop. (4) No allowed-sides parameter: ml_entry does not call the existing _resolve_side_filter (side_filter / long_only), and nothing is per account. (5) Cost basis: tau and pred net R were fit net of the CRYPTO cost stack (fee 11 + slip 3 bps rt + funding 1 bps/8h); there is no per-account cost basis. (6) Features assume 24 bars/day (ret_168, vol168, hour/dow). Equity 1h series differ in distribution: an EVIDENCE question, not code. A roster add on alpaca_live needs its own Stage-0 record (roster-promotion-evidence-guard C1-C5) on the equity population. DONE WHEN: one ml_entry implementation takes per-account (or per-leg-per-account) reference source, anchor, sides, session/cadence and cost basis from config, with tests; plus an evidence record for the first non-crypto account. Gates: none. 2026-11-01 ~18:00Z GENERAL RULE (operator, relayed by Manager Session 2026-11-01a): a general ML trades every market it is validated on and that our venues list. Operator verbatim ~17:55Z: "if the ML passed on other coins, then it can trade other coins. It doesn't need to be restricted to coins we're already trading if those other coins are available on the platforms that we're trading." Operator verbatim ~18:00Z: "let me know if there's any blockers to it trading other coins that it passed on. If we need to do some tests on the paper account to make sure that those trades go through correctly, then we need to get on that as soon as possible ... If we have an ML that's general ML ... it needs to be trading all of those things." Applied first to ml_entry on bybit_2 + bybit_portfolio: universe = the c692-01 held-out population that Bybit lists as a USDT perp (branch claude/ml-entry-universe-widen).  | 2026-11-03 ~10:45Z OPERATOR (chat, Manager Session 2026-11-03a), verbatim: "for the alpaca build, we can hold off until after the reset. We just don't really have capacity for that ... we'll have to build it over the weekend, and we'll only be able to test it next Monday, but we can have that as a plan now." PLAN: build after the Wed 11-04 18:00Z reset (weekend), first alpaca_live test Mon 2026-11-09. Also verbatim: "if we need to create separate variations of the ML entry for different accounts ... we can keep fine-tuning that and testing different variations, and ones that are more specific, ones that are less specific ... still working towards the end goal of having the one model that just does everything on all ... the accounts, but we also want to keep the more specific variations so that we can compare those results over time ... we can hold that off until planning." -> Thursday 11-05 planning item: how general vs account/category-specific ML entry variants are run and compared.  | 2026-11-03 ~10:50Z OPERATOR REVISED (verbatim): "Sorry for Alpaca, I do want to change the timeline there. I realized I was wrong. If we can get that going Wednesday night, then maybe we can get it trading by Thursday evening or Friday and be able to see some stuff before the weekend." PLAN: dispatch the build at the Wed 11-04 18:00Z reset (first item of the reset protocol's after_reset work); target first alpaca_live ml_entry trade Thu 11-05 evening / Fri 11-06. OPERATOR 2026-11-04 ~19:04Z, verbatim: "when we put the ML entry on our account, it can create it's not limited to what's on the roster. It's roster is whatever data it trained on or whatever it can put it trade on. ... the roster includes the strategies ... one of the strategies in the configuration is the ML entry, but the configuration doesn't specify what trades. It doesn't specify like what coins or what security trades. It just specifies which strategies, including which MLs, are active on that account. That's it." => ml_entry traded universe = model-scorable instruments x venue-tradable, NOT strategies.yaml ml_entry.symbols/account_symbols (today 5 coins on bybit_2/bybit_portfolio, 13 ETFs on alpaca_paper).
